draft.title: Describing an association
card: Direction
Positive: as one variable increases, the other tends to increase. Negative: as one increases, the other tends to decrease. No direction: no clear trend.
Form
Linear if the points follow a straight line pattern. Non-linear if they follow a curve.
Strength
Strong if the points sit close to a clear pattern. Weak if they are widely scattered around it. Moderate sits in between.
A strong association does not prove that one variable causes the other. Both may be affected by a third variable, or the link may be coincidence.

1.alt: A scatterplot of hours of practice against test score for 12 students. Each dot is one student. As the hours of practice increase, the scores tend to increase, so the direction is positive.

draft.remember: Describe direction, form and strength. A strong association does not prove cause.

a.q: The points on a scatterplot fall from left to right and sit close to a straight line. Which description fits best?
a.why: Points sloping down show a negative direction. A straight line pattern is linear, and points close to the line make it strong. Positive is wrong because the other variable decreases as the first increases.
a.clue: Read the points from left to right: do they rise or fall?

b.q: Daily ice cream sales and sunburn cases in Melbourne have a strong positive linear association. What can we conclude?
opts: Neither variable is shown to cause the other
Ice cream sales are shown to cause sunburn cases
Sunburn cases are shown to cause ice cream sales
The association is weak, as neither causes the other
b.why: A strong association does not prove cause. A third variable, such as hot sunny weather, may affect both. Saying ice cream sales cause sunburn is tempting, but strength only describes how close the points sit to the pattern.
b.clue: Think about what else could affect both variables on a hot day.

b.best: Neither variable is shown to cause the other

proposal.title: Scatterplots and association
card: A scatterplot shows two numerical variables measured on the same individuals. Each dot is one individual, with one variable on each axis.
Direction
Positive: as one variable increases, the other tends to increase. Negative: as one increases, the other tends to decrease. No direction: no clear trend.
Form
Linear if the points follow a straight line pattern. Non-linear if they follow a curve.
Strength
Strong if the points sit close to a clear pattern. Weak if they are widely scattered around it. Moderate sits in between.

2.alt: A scatterplot of hours of practice against test score for 12 students. Each dot is one student. As the hours of practice increase, the scores tend to increase, so the direction is positive.

proposal.remember: Describe an association by its direction, its form and its strength.

a.q: The points on a scatterplot fall from left to right and sit close to a straight line. Which description fits best?
a.why: Points sloping down show a negative direction. A straight line pattern is linear, and points close to the line make it strong. Positive is wrong because the other variable decreases as the first increases.
a.clue: Read the points from left to right: do they rise or fall?

b.q: Ravi records the age and resale value of 10 used cars in Geelong. Which description fits his scatterplot?
b.why: Value falls as age rises, so the direction is negative. The points drop steeply and then level off, which is a curve, so the form is non-linear, and they sit close to that curve, so it is strong. Linear is tempting, but a straight line would miss the bend.
b.clue: Does the pattern drop by the same amount each year?

fig.alt: A scatterplot of car age in years against resale value in thousands of dollars for 10 cars. The values are 33 at 1 year, 26 at 2, 21 at 3, 16 at 4, 13 at 5, 11 at 6, 9 at 7, 8 at 8, 7 at 9 and 6 at 10. The values fall quickly at first, then level off, with the dots close to a smooth curve.
